title: Note Book of an English Opium-Eater
sourceTitle: Note Book of an English Opium-Eater
author: Thomas De Quincey
description: "The Note Book of an English Opium-Eater" by Thomas De Quincey is a collection of essays and reflections written in the early 19th century.
longDescription: The work grapples with deep and often unsettling themes, including the aesthetics of murder and the complex interplay of horror and beauty, as evidenced by De Quincey’s exploration of notorious historical events, notably the infamous Ratcliffe Highway murders.

authorInfo.bio: Thomas Penson De Quincey was an English writer, essayist, and literary critic, best known for his Confessions of an English Opium-Eater (1821). Many scholars suggest that in publishing this work De Quincey inaugurated the tradition of addiction literature in the Western world.
